title: Raga Prabhati
hookLine: the Granth turns from evening to daybreak, and Guru Nanak's first Prabhati hymn names what to put on before anything else

lines: A HYMN ABOUT WHAT TO WEAR.
cards: What's the first thing you put on in the morning? Glasses, maybe. A watch, a ring from the nightstand.
A turban, tied fresh, fold by fold, before the house is awake. Whatever it is, it goes on before the day can ask anything of you. For two days the Granth has been in the evening.
Now it turns a page and the sky is getting light. The raga is Prabhati, tradition sings it at dawn, and Guru Nanak opens it with something to wear.

teach.b: In the Granth's order, Prabhati follows Kalyan. Hymns of the Gurus open it, then come Bhagats whose words the Gurus set beside their own, Kabir among them.
Tradition sings Prabhati at the edge of light; teachers describe raga moods differently, so take the timing as tradition, not as a rule in the text. The text is Guru Nanak's opening hymn.
In paraphrase: by your Name we cross over. Your Name is honor, and it is worship.
Your Name is my ornament, and the aim of my understanding. Without the Name, there is never honor.

Then the Rahao: all other cleverness is only show; whoever you forgive, their work is made complete. An ornament is the thing you put on so it's seen, the finishing touch. Guru Nanak gives that word to the Name.
So in the dawn raga, the first thing to put on isn't a watch or a ring. It's remembering.
Sikhs call the hours before dawn amrit vela, the ambrosial time, and in the Japji, Guru Nanak links that hour with the true Name and reflection on greatness. Prabhati sings into the same hour.
Hear the Rahao in the morning, too. Early is when the mind starts planning: what to say, how to win, how to look. The hymn doesn't throw planning away.
It puts it second. First the Name, the ornament. Then the day.

how: Sikh practice treasures the early hours, amrit vela, for reciting Gurbani; in some gurdwaras the morning kirtan includes shabads sung in Raga Prabhati.

o: a morning prayer said only on festival days
a drum rhythm played to wake the gurdwara
the dawn raga, opening with the Name as an ornament

games.q: what's inside Raga Prabhati — tap the pairs.

s: Prabhati's opening hymn gives the ornament to the Name
your Name is my ornament, and the aim of my understanding.
Prabhati holds only the Gurus' hymns
Bhagats' hymns follow the Gurus', Kabir among them.
the hymn says all planning is wrong
it calls other cleverness only show; the Name comes first, the day after.

games.q: it's dawn and Guru Nanak is naming the ornament worth wearing. what does the hymn choose?
o: a clever plan for the day.
games.why: your Name is my ornament, the hymn says, and the Rahao adds: all other cleverness is only show.

practice: Sit as if it were early, the house quiet, the light thin, the breath slow and even, and if you can, play a shabad sung in Raga Prabhati.
Before any plan for the day takes shape, let the first thing you put on be something other than a plan: if you pray, Waheguru, said once on the breath; if you don't, a minute of simple attention.
When the clever thoughts arrive, let them wait at the door.

wordCard.voice: Raga Prabhati. The raga that follows Kalyan, which tradition sings at daybreak, opening with Guru Nanak's hymn: your Name is my ornament, and all other cleverness is only show. Today's word.

orig.note: the dawn raga's name as it appears in the Granth's heading, Raag Prabhati.

carryVoice: Your line: dawn. The Name goes on first, like an ornament, before any cleverness. Until tomorrow.
